passage.title: Rocket to the Moon
passage.text:
Leo transformed a cardboard box into a rocket by covering it with foil — the same material used on real spacecraft to reflect the Sun's heat. He cut three round windows and checked that his control panel of buttons still worked.

“Ten, nine, eight…” Leo counted down to one and imagined lift-off. In his mind, gravity pulled less and less as the rocket climbed higher, until his body felt almost weightless.

Space has no air, so Leo's astronaut helmet carried its own oxygen supply. Looking back, he saw Earth as a single blue and green sphere — smaller than he expected, with no borders between countries visible at all.

The Moon's surface was covered in craters — bowl-shaped hollows formed by rocks crashing into it millions of years ago. “Leo, dinner!” called Mum, and just like that, the mission was complete.
